demonstrated_gap: The gap is search target recall. The retained Tavily session missed the intended NautilusTrader adapter guide (evidence/receipts/native-tavily-session-20260920.json line 83: intended_adapter_guide_found=false). On an open 100-task documentation benchmark averaged over three runs, Exa search+fetch completed 81.7±1.1 (auto) and 83.0±1.0 (deep) against Tavily's 59.0±1.7 (basic) and 60.0±2.0 (advanced). Search-only, Exa fast scored 66.3±1.5 against Tavily basic at 51.0±5.3. A separate 100-query general benchmark scores Exa 14.39 and Tavily 13.67, a difference that is not statistically significant. Exa's hosted MCP works anonymously with rate limits through web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa, so a trial through native `claude mcp add` or `codex mcp add` needs no new credential and no local standing stack. Caveats: the service is hosted and cannot be version-pinned, queries leave the host exactly as with Tavily, and the docs-benchmark repository was forked by a web-data API vendor (String), so its independence is not established.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Freeze a query set of at least 30 queries with pre-registered target URLs, including the NautilusTrader adapter-guide query Tavily missed, plus IBKR, Alpaca, SEC and arXiv targets. Run three passes each through Exa (anonymous hosted MCP: web_search_exa, then web_fetch_exa) and tvly search/extract, on both hosts. Measure target-URL recall@5, correct-source citation rate, extraction completeness against the trafilatura gold set, latency, and anonymous rate-limit failures. Exa replaces Tavily for search only if its recall@5 is higher beyond run-to-run variance and it needs no credential. The decision is overturned if recall comes within noise or anonymous limits make runs fail.

demonstrated_gap: There is no current gap: the requirement has no crawl or ingestion task, and extraction quality is better targeted by the trafilatura trial, which has independent benchmarks and needs no server. The decisive reason is supply-chain health. The GitHub Advisory Database lists 10 Crawl4AI advisories published 2026-06-16 to 2026-06-21, 5 critical and 5 high. They include unauthenticated RCE via Chromium launch-argument injection (GHSA-r253-r9jw-qg44), a pre-auth AST sandbox escape (GHSA-qxjp-w3pj-48m7), an auth bypass through a hardcoded default JWT signing key (GHSA-8qrg-7j2f-rf2h), and path traversal in crawler downloads leading to RCE (GHSA-2jq4-q6vv-4cp3). All are fixed by 0.9.0; the current release is v0.9.4.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Reconsider only if a defined multi-page crawl or ingestion requirement appears that agent-browser plus trafilatura cannot meet, and Crawl4AI shows at least two consecutive releases with no new advisories in library (non-Docker) mode. It would then need to beat that pair on the frozen URL set for completeness and F1.

demonstrated_gap: No one has measured how well the current lane extracts attributable text. For HTML pages that serve no markdown or llms.txt, the `read` command in the pinned winner agent-browser v0.38.1 falls back to html_to_markdownish. That function strips only script, style, noscript, svg and head (cli/src/read.rs line 1045, byte-identical on main), so nav, header, footer and aside boilerplate reaches the agent, and no extraction-accuracy evidence exists for it. The other extraction path, tvly extract, is a hosted service that needs a credential, backed by only two retained single-URL extractions. Trafilatura is a local Apache-2.0 library and CLI. It outputs TXT, Markdown or JSON with title, author, date and site-name metadata that supports attribution. It has independent evidence: WCXB held-out F1 0.841 (second of seven; dev F1 0.888 on documentation pages) against Readability at 0.736, and Bevendorff et al. 2023 named it the best single tool by mean ROUGE-LSum F1. It needs no credential, runs as a plain CLI on both hosts, and can read agent-browser-rendered HTML for JS-heavy pages.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Freeze at least 30 primary-source URLs covering the layer's real targets: NautilusTrader docs including the adapter guide Tavily missed, IBKR and Alpaca API docs, SEC EDGAR filing pages, arXiv abstract pages and vendor changelogs. On linux-wsl2 and macOS, run `agent-browser read`, `tvly extract` and `trafilatura --markdown --with-metadata`, the last on both fetched HTML and agent-browser-rendered HTML. Score word-level F1 against hand-verified main-content gold, key-passage recall, output tokens and wall time. Adopt trafilatura as the extraction lane only if it beats agent-browser read's HTML fallback beyond run variance on non-markdown pages without losing key passages. The decision is overturned if agent-browser read (markdown/llms.txt path plus fallback) comes within noise, or if Tavily Extract is materially more complete on JS-heavy pages.

demonstrated_gap: The requirement calls for bounded native commands, and the GPT-6 runtime already installed on both hosts has a first-party search tool that no layer evidence compares with the Tavily winner. Codex `web_search` defaults to 'cached', an OpenAI-maintained index with no external web access. It also offers 'indexed' (PR #28489, merged 2026-06-19) and 'live' modes, and `tools.web_search` accepts allowed_domains and context_size. `codex exec --json` emits WebSearchItem {id, query, action, results}, carrying structured results when available, so retrieval is observable and attributable in the JSONL stream. If native search, run alongside Claude Code's native WebSearch as a second native arm, reaches Tavily's target recall, the separate Tavily credential and CLI become optional for search. No measured quality evidence for Codex web search on documentation targets was found, so the trial itself must supply it.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the same frozen target-URL query set through `codex exec --json` with web_search set to cached and then live (with allowed_domains unset, then scoped), and through Claude Code's native WebSearch. Measure target-URL recall@5 from the WebSearchItem results and final citations, the stale-result rate in cached mode, the presence of attributable URLs in JSONL, latency, and complete provider usage. The decision is overturned if native recall is below Tavily's beyond variance, or if the JSONL results lack attributable URLs.

demonstrated_gap: Two 2026 benchmarks place Firecrawl above Tavily. On documentation tasks it scores 76.0±1.0 search+fetch against Tavily's 59-60, and 70.3±1.5 search-only (#2); AIMultiple scores it 14.58 (#2, statistically tied with the top four). The CLI also bundles a research-paper index (`firecrawl research search-papers`) that overlaps OpenResearch, and it ships official skills. It is not a trial now for four reasons. It needs a new Firecrawl account or API key (hosted credits), or a self-hosted AGPL-3.0 Firecrawl stack (a standing service) reached through --api-url. Its license is declared only as ISC in package.json; the repository has no LICENSE file and GitHub reports none. Its `init` command installs skills globally into every detected agent unless scoped with --agent. Exa's anonymous endpoint can test the same search gap without a credential.

Put `firecrawl search` and `firecrawl scrape` (hosted free credits or a self-hosted --api-url) through the same target-URL recall@5, citation and extraction-F1 scoring, three runs on both hosts. Promote it only if it beats Tavily and Exa beyond variance at acceptable per-query cost, and after upstream adds a LICENSE file.

demonstrated_gap: It is the only credible candidate offering keyless search and fetch that return verbatim excerpts pinned to byte-offset source spans, which addresses attribution directly, with local caching and no account. It would remove the Tavily credential and aligns with the local-first principle. It is not a trial now: it is a v0.2.x beta, and its only comparison is a single-query demo (n=1) against WebSearch, Tavily and Exa. Its search relies on 18 direct adapters to public engines, which carries reliability and terms risk. `npx wigolo init` downloads a browser engine and on-device models (about 1.5 GB). It bundles research and agent loops (LLM key or Ollama) that would have to stay disabled under the no-standing-research-stack requirement. It is dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 with a request that companies buy a commercial license, and GitHub reports its license as NOASSERTION.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run keyless `wigolo search --json` and `wigolo fetch` (research/agent disabled) over the same frozen query set and URL set on both hosts, repeated on three or more days. Measure target recall@5 against Tavily and Exa, the engine-failure rate, byte-offset span verification against the retrieved bytes, and fetch F1 against trafilatura. Promote it to a trial only if recall matches, spans verify exactly, and engine failures stay low across days.
